item.text: The same mistake appears in the original controls and was copied into Compact: visual classes are managed separately from React state. The view buttons also remove their highlight without restoring it. I’ll make these classes render from state, delete the timer helper, and replace the contributing guidance that told agents to use it. Regression tests will check the classes immediately after state changes.

/bin/bash -lc "cat > src/visualState.test.tsx <<'EOF'
import '@testing-library/jest-dom/vitest'
import { afterEach, expect, it } from 'vitest'
import { cleanup, fireEvent, render, screen } from '@testing-library/react'
import { App } from './App'
import { StatusBadge } from './StatusBadge'
import { SyncIndicator } from './SyncIndicator'

afterEach(cleanup)

it('renders compact classes with the toggle state immediately', () => {
  render(<App />)
  const button = screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Compact' })
  const panel = screen.getByRole('main')
  expect(button).not.toHaveClass('is-active')
  expect(panel).not.toHaveClass('compact')
  for (const active of [true, false, true]) {
    fireEvent.click(button)
    expect(button).toHaveAttribute('aria-pressed', String(active))
    expect(button.classList.contains('is-active')).toBe(active)
    expect(panel.classList.contains('compact')).toBe(active)
  }
})

it('keeps selection, priority, view, and focus classes in sync with interactions', () => {
  render(<App />)
  const inbox = screen.getByTestId('folder-inbox')
  const sent = screen.getByTestId('folder-sent')
  expect(inbox).toHaveClass('is-active')
  fireEvent.click(sent)
  expect(sent).toHaveClass('is-active')
  expect(inbox).not.toHaveClass('is-active')
  fireEvent.click(inbox)
  expect(inbox).toHaveClass('is-active')
  expect(sent).not.toHaveClass('is-active')

  const priority = screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Priority only' })
  for (const active of [true, false]) {
    fireEvent.click(priority)
    expect(priority.classList.contains('is-active')).toBe(active)
  }

  const list = screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'List' })
  const preview = screen.getByRole('button', { name: 'Preview' })
  expect(list).toHaveClass('is-active')
  fireEvent.click(preview)
  expect(preview).toHaveClass('is-active')
  expect(list).not.toHaveClass('is-active')
  fireEvent.click(list)
  expect(list).toHaveClass('is-active')
  expect(preview).not.toHaveClass('is-active')

  const search = screen.getByRole('searchbox')
  fireEvent.focus(search)
  expect(search).toHaveClass('is-focused')
  fireEvent.blur(search)
  expect(search).not.toHaveClass('is-focused')
})

it('renders unread and online classes from current props', () => {
  const { rerender } = render(<><StatusBadge count={3} /><SyncIndicator online /></>)
  expect(screen.getByTestId('unread-badge')).toHaveClass('has-unread')
  expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveClass('is-online')
  rerender(<><StatusBadge count={0} /><SyncIndicator online={false} /></>)
  expect(screen.getByTestId('unread-badge')).not.toHaveClass('has-unread')
  expect(screen.getByRole('status')).not.toHaveClass('is-online')
  rerender(<><StatusBadge count={1} /><SyncIndicator online /></>)
  expect(screen.getByTestId('unread-badge')).toHaveClass('has-unread')
  expect(screen.getByRole('status')).toHaveClass('is-online')
})
EOF

item.text:
Fixed one repeated class: visual classes drifting from React state, present in the original controls and copied into Compact.

- Removed the timer helper and rendered all visual classes directly from state or props.
- Added regression tests; all three fail against the actual past implementation and pass now.
- Replaced misleading guidance and added the enforcement table and CI checks.

Architecture was the highest applicable fix; tests guard the observable behavior. `npm run check` passes.

Changes remain uncommitted because `.git` is read-only.
